A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EgoDTM research. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A–D, which were also inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, action-recognition, depth-estimation, robot-manipulation, localization, and ablation results in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds moment-query evaluation in Table 4 and expanded downstream component ablations in Table 7.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same dual encoders, adaptive-bin depth decoder, HOID–SAM2–LLM caption pipeline, joint objectives, and inference procedure. The appendix supplies implementation and prompting details without establishing a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds EK100CLS action-classification evaluation and EgoMQ video-only temporal activity localization, with results in Tables 7 and 4 respectively. These extend task coverage within existing datasets beyond v1's retrieval, EGTEA recognition, depth, robotics, and language-query evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained retrieval, depth, robotics, NLQ, and VISOR comparisons. The added MQ benchmark reuses EgoVLP, LaViLa, and AVION from the existing localization comparison. Newly discussed ImageBind, LanguageBind, and VGGT are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a VSGN-based evaluation procedure for EgoMQ and top-1/top-5 evaluation for EK100CLS. Its expanded component experiments additionally report EgoNLQ mIoU and EgoMQ mAP, extending the evaluation design beyond the retained recall-based comparisons. Existing pretraining settings remain unchanged; Appendix A's newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Table 7 extends depth/text component ablations beyond retrieval to EK100CLS, EgoNLQ, EgoMQ, and depth estimation, testing whether component benefits transfer across tasks. Figure 4 adds a qualitative comparison of inconsistent detections and temporally consistent masks. The six original ablations remain in Table 6, while the RGB-plus-depth recognition analysis survives only as a textual summary without its original numerical table.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 newly reports two random seeds and averaging of success rates for robot manipulation. v1 provides no corresponding seed information. This is additional disclosure, not evidence that the number of runs increased; confidence intervals, error bars, and significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: The retained headline comparisons and original ablation values are unchanged. New results include MQ R5@0.3 of 50.08 for EgoDTM versus 48.68 for LaViLa in Table 4, and classification, localization, and depth component results in Table 7. Conversely, v1 Table 7's RGB/RGB+Depth scores, including top-1 accuracies of 68.2/69.5, are omitted from v2 although Appendix B retains the improvement claim.

T1.justification: The depth-bin definitions, depth-map construction, and loss equations remain mathematically unchanged in Equations 1–7. Neither version provides additional theorems or proofs, and v2's new empirical metrics do not introduce formal theoretical developments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: depth-aware pretraining and spatially enriched captions improve egocentric representations through a lightweight decoder and data-generation pipeline. The new experiments support these existing claims without redefining the principal contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly acknowledges that depth pretraining can hurt EgoNLQ and proposes proxy-task bias to explain opposing changes in scale-aware and scale-invariant depth errors. Appendix D adds a real-world deployment rationale despite weaker simulation performance than specialized manipulation models. The conclusion also adds directions involving multimodal language models and richer 3D supervision.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C newly document narration filtering, frame sampling, dataset splits, inference crops, depth-probe optimization, robot trajectories and viewpoints, NLQ feature processing, and the detailed LLM prompt and size thresholds. These substantially expand reproducibility information without demonstrating altered settings. However, Table 1 removes per-method supervision, text-volume, and parameter-count columns. The abstract also replaces its future code-release wording with a 'Code:' link.

R1.justification: Appendix D adds a focused comparison with ImageBind and LanguageBind, distinguishing depth prediction from treating depth as an aligned input modality. New citations also cover VGGT, VSGN, DINOv2, and implementation background. The main related-work discussion and overall novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence are retained. v2 introduces organized appendices and acknowledgments, moves the multimodal-depth and robot-case discussions into the supplement, expands component interpretation, separates quantitative and qualitative HOI discussion, and updates affiliations.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column conference format and substantially rearranges displays. It adds MQ and downstream-ablation tables plus HOI-comparison, prompting, and generated-data figures. The robot illustration moves from Figure 4 to appendix Figure 6; the RGB/depth table and several Table 1 metadata columns disappear.

improvement.justification: The expanded component ablations provide more informative evidence, including negative transfer, while the new task evaluation and detailed appendix improve validation and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the reporting losses, but the omitted RGB/depth results table, removed comparison metadata, and Appendix B's unresolved table reference limit the net improvement.
